prem_087ca827f2bab1ac.text: Published analyses of spinach's iron content from the early twentieth century reported a value approximately ten times higher than the amount measured by later analyses.

prem_090b41644a0a0b84.text: Raw spinach contains roughly 2.7 mg of iron per 100 g, a level comparable to other common leafy green vegetables rather than exceptional among foods.

prem_40d02a12cd2d1d5c.text: The tenfold overstatement of spinach's iron content in the nutrition literature originated from a decimal point placed one position too far to the right when the original measurement was recorded or transcribed.

prem_7589ccd15d6f57a2.text: The overstated iron figure for spinach was reproduced in food composition tables, textbooks, and popular media for decades before being corrected.

prem_d3957a8b1132fa0c.text: Popular belief that spinach is an exceptionally iron-rich food emerged after the erroneous figure entered circulation and was not supported by any independent measurement showing unusually high iron in spinach.

prem_da1136f4cfd04299.text: A food is famous as iron-rich when the public widely believes it to contain unusually high amounts of iron relative to other foods.

root_claim.text: A misplaced decimal point made spinach famous as an iron-rich food.
